data.name: Caiophas
data.gender_notes: Caiophas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Biblical times, the name Caiophas was given to the Jewish high priest who oversaw the temple in Jerusalem. The name is derived from the Hebrew words 'kaph' meaning 'to carry' and 'paz' meaning 'burden' or 'release'. Caiophas was the high priest at the time of Jesus' trial and ultimately played a significant role in his crucifixion.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the burden of responsibility and the release of sin through faith in Christ.
data.etymology: Caiophas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Burden carrier.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Caiophas total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: קאיופאס
in_hebrew.meaning: השם קאיופאס נגזר מהמילה העברית כיפאס שפירושו קצר רוח
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קאיופאס הוא גרסה עברית של השם היווני Καιάφας (Kайафаs), שמקורו בשם העברי כיפאס. כיפאס נגזר מהמילה כף, שפירושו קצר רוח או קפדן. השם קאיופאס מזכיר את קאייפאס, הכוהן הגדול ששפט את ישו במשפטו לפני צליפתו. במשך ההיסטוריה, השם קאיופאס נשא משמעות של כוח רוחני וסמכות דתית.

in_greek.name: Καιάφας
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Καιάφας σημαίνει αυτός που είναι αυστηρός ή σύντομος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καιάφας είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος כיפאס (Kapha's), που σημαίνει αυστηρός ή σύντομος. Στο Ευαγγέλιο του Ιωάννη (11:49, 18:13-14), ο Καιάφας αναφέρεται ως ο αρχιερέας που συνέλαβε και δίκασε τον Ιησού. Η χρήση του ονόματος Καιάφας στην Εκκλησία των Πρώτων Χριστιανών αντανακλά τη σχέση του με την κρίση και τη σταύρωση του Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Caiophas
in_latin.meaning: Caiophas significat stricto animo vel brevis spiritus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Caiophas derivatur ex hebraeo כיפאס (Kapha's), quod significat stricto animo vel brevis spiritus. In Ecclesia primitiva, Caiophas fuit summus sacerdos qui Iesum Christum iudicavit. Hoc nomen in traditione christiana saepe refertur ad auctoritatem et potestatem spiritualem.

in_english.name: Caiophas
in_english.meaning: Caiophas means strict or short-tempered, derived from Hebrew
in_english.long_meaning: The name Caiophas originates from the Hebrew name כיפאס (Kapha's), meaning strict or short-tempered. It is best known from the New Testament as the name of Caiaphas, the high priest who presided over the trial of Jesus Christ. Throughout Christian history, Caiophas has symbolized spiritual authority and strict judgment. The name is associated with leadership and decision-making, reflecting its biblical significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Caiophas holds cultural significance to the Christian faith as it represents the high priest who was a key player in the religious and political events leading up to Jesus' crucifixion. This figure, well known in the Bible and in Christian history, is a reminder of the tensions between the religious authorities and the messianic movement that Jesus represented, and how these tensions ultimately led to his death.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Caiophas serves as a reminder of the role of free will and the importance of bearing burdens and releasing them. The name represents the high priest's role in overseeing the temple and the spiritual community in Jerusalem, and his ultimately playing a part in releasing Jesus to fulfill his destiny as the crucified savior. Additionally, Caiophas's name derives from words meaning 'to carry' and 'burden,' which can be seen as a reminder of Jesus' own experience of carrying the cross and bearing the burden of sin for all of mankind.02:03
data.spiritual_symbolism: Caiaphas was the high priest in Jerusalem during the time of Jesus' crucifixion. His name means 'the god of loving kindness' or 'replacing kindness'. However, despite this name, Caiaphas was instrumental in orchestrating the plot against Jesus, ultimately leading to His crucifixion. This paradoxical juxtaposition of a spiritual name with an unspiritual act highlights the complexities of human nature and the struggle between good and evil.

biblical_reference.note: Caiaphas was the high priest who sentenced Jesus to death.

historical_references.reference: According to the New Testament, Caiaphas was the high priest of the Temple in Jerusalem during the time of Jesus' trial and execution. The Gospel of John reports that Caiaphas made the prophetic statement, 'It is expedient for us that one man should die for the people.' (John 11:49-52)
historical_references.context: During the rule of Roman procurators in Judea, the high priest was appointed by the Roman authorities. Caiaphas was likely appointed around 18-26 AD and held the position until his death around 36 AD.

historical_references.reference: The Jewish historian Josephus mentions Caiaphas in his works and provides some additional context about his role in Jewish political affairs. According to Josephus, Caiaphas was a prominent member of the Sanhedrin, the supreme council of Jewish leaders. He is noted for his opposition to Roman rule and his efforts to maintain Jewish autonomy, which may have contributed to the conflict with Jesus and the Romans.
historical_references.context: The Sanhedrin, or Great Assembly, was the supreme council of Jewish leaders in Jerusalem. Caiaphas was a member of this council and may have held the position of high priest during his tenure. His opposition to Roman rule and his efforts to maintain Jewish autonomy made him a significant figure in Jewish politics during the late Second Temple period.

modern_usage.modern_context: In religious studies, Caiaphas is well-known as the high priest who presided over the trial of Jesus before the Sanhedrin. In biblical archaeology, Caiaphas is a subject of ongoing research due to his prominence in the New Testament. In historical fiction, Caiaphas has been a popular character in various novels and films, such as 'The Last Temptation of Christ' and 'Mary Magdalene'. The modern context of Caiaphas' name is often associated with these fields and the historical narrative they contribute.
